name: adv_junction_fluid_node_h_is_equality
source:
// Two inflows of DIFFERENT enthalpy meeting on a raw connect node. If the node
// equates h (rather than flow-weighting it) this document is inconsistent —
// which is exactly what it is written to reveal.
COMPONENT StreamIn(out)
  PARAM mdot, h
  out.mdot = -mdot
  out.h    = h
END
COMPONENT PressureOut(in)
  PARAM P
  in.P = P
END
StreamIn    A(mdot = 1.0, h = 100000)
StreamIn    B(mdot = 3.0, h = 400000)
PressureOut C(P = 200000)
connect(A.out, B.out, C.in)
hc = C.in.h
mc = C.in.mdot
pa = A.out.P

error.message: There are 13 equations and 12 variables. The problem is overspecified and cannot be solved. Redundant relation (no free variable left to determine): CONNECT a.out, b.out, c.in: a$out.h = b$out.h. A common cause: the same physics stated twice — a boundary pinning a quantity a component already defines (a re-equated mixer pressure, a T-pinned wall state), or two property calls restating one relation.
